newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bakun dam IPO underwriting pact to be signed.
newsitem.headline: Bakun dam IPO underwriting pact to be signed.

text.p: Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd will sign an underwriting agreement for its pending initial public offering (IPO) on Tuesday, taking a first step toward its mammoth 1.5 billion stock issue.

Bakun Hydro-Electric, the holding company for the $5.4 billion dam being built in the rainforests of Sarawak state on Borneo island, said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad will witness the signing of the pact.
The ceremony, at 11 a.m. local time (0300 GMT), will involve 53 institutions, a spokeswoman for the event said on Monday.

Mahathir has been one of the biggest defenders of the project, which has drawn fire from environmentalists and tribals who will be displaced by the construction. The dam has a capacity of 2,400 megawatts and is due to be completed by 2003.
It will clear 69,000 hectares (170,500 acres) of forest and create a reservoir the size of Singapore.
The IPO is a crucial financing element for the project. Of the 1.5 billion shares, 375 million will be offered to the public at 2.00 ringgit a share.
Talk had emerged recently in the Malaysian stock market that foreign investors were balking at the IPO, due to doubts about the investment's returns.
The main adviser to the IPO denied the speculation.
Ekran Bhd is the main contractor of the project, and will hold about 32 percent of Bakun's shares.
The rest will be divided among various Sarawak state and federal government agencies, with 25 percent of the offering sold to foreign and local institutions.
Bakun's stock is expected to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in June.
